thread:
jess: Customer report: when they use JSON mode + streaming we see intermittent invalid JSON. body sometimes has partial objects, extra keys injected between items, and items appear out of order. example payload attached below. customer org: org-53421, affected endpoint: /v1/responses, model: redwood-13b-v1.

maria: thanks @jess — can you paste the raw response they got? any request_id or trace id? also SDK / server-side proxy versions?

jess: pasted raw (redacted):
```
{"items":[{"id":"1","value":"a"},{"id":"2","value":"b"}
{"temp_id":"t-xx","aux":null}
,{"id":"3","value":"c"}]
```
When parsed client-side this fails with JSON parse error. Customer says sometimes the `temp_id` chunk shows up between item objects and some items are missing fields.

sam: hmm looks like streaming chunks got interleaved. Do we have any logs for request_id=rx-8a7?

eng-bot: log lookup complete for rx-8a7: stream_chunks: [chunk-1(seq=1), chunk-3(seq=3), chunk-2(seq=2)] 
parser: JSONModeParserError: Unexpected token '{' at position 84
batcher: reordered 3->2 due to late arrival

maria: customer running a very aggressive proxy that opens multiple parallel connections and reorders TCP packets? they say they're on our hosted API, no proxy documented. SDK v0.9.1.

alex_r: assigning to @sam and @alex_r to triage ordering. first guess: streaming boundary splits a record and our client-side recombination relies on sequence ordering that can be disrupted by HTTP/2 multiplexing or a buggy reverse proxy.

maria: reproduced locally with `curl --http2` through a dev proxy that simulates out-of-order chunks. when I set streaming=false, output is stable.

jess: customer is seeing billing spikes because they retry on parse errors. billing-bot: flagged potential duplicate charges for rx-8a7 and rx-8b9 — please capture full request ids so we can reconcile.

billing-bot: preliminary: 3 charged attempts for org-53421 within 90s for same client op. mark for manual review.

sam: quick mitigation we can ask customer: 1) disable streaming (stream:false) 2) upgrade SDK to 0.9.3 which adds chunk-sequence headers and reassembly on client 3) ensure any proxy preserves chunk order and doesn't multiplex responses.

maria: I'll send those instructions and request full traces + curl reproduction steps. also asking customer if they can try `Connection: close` to avoid multiplexing.

jess: attaching repro steps we sent to customer:
```
# reproduce (simulating out-of-order)
python simulate_reorder.py --model redwood-13b-v1 --stream --reorder 3,1,2
# client should fail to parse without sequence headers
```

alex_r: engineering note: runtime will harden streaming boundaries. action items: (1) add sequence index to every chunk in streaming protocol (2) server-side sanity check to buffer until full top-level array close for JSON mode (3) add analytics flag when JSONModeParserError occurs for same org to auto-detect regressions.

sam: I'll own the runtime changes, expect initial PR by EOD tomorrow. tagging @eng-bot to create a ticket.

eng-bot: ticket created: RFC-8342 streaming-chunk-seq-and-buffering. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RFC-8342 :eyes:

maria: customer OK with mitigation for now. asked for invoice hold while billing team verifies duplicate charges.

billing-bot: added hold on org-53421 pending manual review.

jess: thanks all. follow-up: once runtime PR lands let's push an opt-in client patch to 0.9.3 and communicate in status page. :thumbsup:
